title: Man. Post. Cap. X: GAR/PLAC — ‘we are naturally under that law’? Prove it
pass_a_gloss: Garissoles flips it: we are naturally under that law; therefore its breach is rightly imputed to us. Placeus asks: are we naturally under that law? Then we are bound to keep it.
pass_b_english: But we conclude in the contrary way.
We are naturally under that law.
Therefore its violation is deservedly imputed to us.
PLAC. Are we naturally under that law?
Then we are bound to observe it.
source_text: Nos vero contrario modo concludimus. Sumus naturaliter sub ea lege. Ergo eius violatio merito nobis imputatur. PLAC. Anne sumus naturaliter sub illa lege? Tenemur igitur eam observare.

choices.choice: GAR: naturally under it → breach imputed; PLAC challenges
